title: VPC Snapshot — Cost-Aware Filtration & Operational Cards
creator: Maya Chen
description: Design a 'VPC Snapshot' panel for the Private Console that surfaces a time-bounded view of a tenant's VPC topology, active cluster links, egress pathways, and cost hotspots. The snapshot supports cost-aware filters, a temporal rewind slider to inspect historical states, and compact operational cards for quick actions (rollback, isolate path, pause upgrade). This ticket contains the prototype, interaction flows, accessibility notes, and handoff artifacts for engineering implementation.
acceptance_criteria: Topology canvas renders <100ms for typical tenant (<=200 nodes) and matches runtime topology data
Cost heatmap displays per-path and per-cluster cost with toggle for normalized units
Filters (cost threshold, region, path type, time window) persist in URL and are shareable
Temporal rewind shows state changes and annotates upgrade/incident events on the timeline
Operational cards provide immediate actions with RBAC checks and clear confirmation flows
Prototype tested and validated with 3 PM stakeholders and 2 SREs for workflow clarity
comments: 2026-02-26 - Maya Chen: Initial sketches uploaded to Figma. Focus is on reducing cognitive load when both topology and cost are visible.

2026-03-03 - Engineering Sync (Priya Rao): Raised concerns about rendering large meshes; recommended progressive disclosure and edge aggregation for >300 links.
2026-03-05 - Accessibility Review (Ravi Singh): Request contrast updates for heatmap palette and keyboard focus indicators for operational cards.
2026-03-10 - Design Critique (Team): Agreed on compact cards, added requirement for low-fidelity printable summary for on-call runbooks.

2026-03-12 - Handoff (Luca Fernandez): Prepared spec for implementation; created TODOs for backend: time-series snapshot endpoint and cost attribution stamp. Linked PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/4821
decisions: Use a horizontal temporal slider with event ticks (upgrades, incidents) rather than a pure dropdown list
Default cost filter resets to 'show hotspots > $0.05/min' to surface actionable issues
Aggregate edges beyond 300 links into 'bundles' with a click-to-expand interaction
Operational cards are context-aware: only show actions the current user can perform (RBAC driven)
tradeoffs: Information density vs clarity: opted for progressive disclosure (summary heatmap + expandable path details) to avoid overwhelming SREs
Client-side rendering vs server-side pre-aggregation: chosen hybrid approach — server returns sampled topology and cost bundles, client expands on demand
Realtime fidelity vs historical alignment: snapshots are eventual (10-30s lag) for large tenants; added explicit timestamp and 'data freshness' indicator
